append.text: **Ps 125:1, 125:4 applied as this row named:** *Quando o Senhor fez voltar o cativeiro de Sião … Fazei voltar, Senhor, o nosso cativeiro*. The ambiguity reader named restoration as the likely hearing but also heard, in both verses, 'make captivity come back upon us' — the risk this row foresaw, now raised by a blind reader. Kept (the row governs 13:7, 52:7, 84:2); *os cativos* (MS1932, CNBB) is the option in Ps 125 — for the main session if the risk is judged real.

**Ps 125:1, 125:3 *facti sumus sicut consoláti … facti sumus lætántes* → *ficamos como consolados … ficamos alegres*** — the stylist's *ficamos* against draft 1's *tornamo-nos* (78:4's form): bookish in the short colon of the Tuesday Vespers antiphon (125:3). One verb twice, as the Latin. The v2 Latinist passed it ('flattens the participle slightly but is defensible'). *tornamo-nos* option.

**Ps 125:2a *Tunc replétum est gáudio os nostrum* → *Então se encheu de júbilo a nossa boca*** — the row followed, as named; the stylist's best line; the ambiguity reader listed *júbilo* as unknown (again). *alegria* option.

**Ps 125:2a, 125:5, 125:6b** — *exsultátio* three times → *exultação* (*de exultação*; *em exultação ceifarão*; *virão com exultação*): *in* → *em* and *cum* → *com* as the Latin has them (the Latinist's minor, taken); the ambiguity reader listed *exultação* as unknown (again), kept. The CNBB's familiar *ceifarão com alegria* is the option.
Ps 125:4 *sicut torrens in Austro* → *como a torrente no sul* (the stylist's generic article); unknown to the ambiguity reader again.
Ps 125:6a *mitténtes sémina sua* → *lançando as suas sementes* — the plural of the sower's seed, D32's plant exception (not offspring).

Ps 125:2b, 3 *Magnificávit Dóminus fácere* (no noun) is rendered *Grandes coisas fez o Senhor* — the same Portuguese as this row's word for another Latin; they never meet. See the new row *magnificáre fácere*.

terms: | magnificáre fácere (cum) | *Grandes coisas fez o Senhor com eles / conosco* | open | Ps 125:2b, 125:3 (ἐμεγάλυνεν … τοῦ ποιῆσαι μετ᾿ αὐτῶν): a verb of making-great with an infinitive, which Portuguese cannot say verb for verb; DRB and MS1932 both 'great things'. *cum* kept as *com / conosco*: the CNBB Liturgia das Horas prints *fez com eles … fez conosco* (verified, `consult/web-lh-salmo-125-126.md`), so the line is known so in Brazil; *por eles / por nós* (DRB, MS1932) option. The same collocation at 125:3 is the Tuesday Vespers antiphon. Passed the Latinist twice. |

| Auster (a region) | sul (*como a torrente no sul*) | open | Ps 125:4 *sicut torrens in Austro*. L&S: first the south wind, by metonymy the south; νότος the same pair. DRB 'in the south', MS1932 'na terra do meio-dia' read the region; Augustine reads the warm wind melting the ice (Enarr. in Ps. 125, `consult/newadvent-augustine-ps125.htm`). The glossary's *o vento sul* (77:26) is where the verb makes the wind plain. The ambiguity reader heard *no sul* as possibly southern Brazil; *no vento sul* is the option. |

| semináre / métere / manípulus | semear / ceifar / feixe (*Os que em lágrimas semeiam, * em exultação ceifarão … trazendo os seus feixes*) | open | Ps 125:5–6; the reaper's verbs, concrete (rule 5). *ceifar* over *colher* (gather) because it goes with the sheaves; the CNBB prints *ceifarão* and *feixes* (verified). *ceifarão*, *feixes* were listed unknown by the ambiguity reader; kept. 128:7 *manum suam qui metit … sinum suum qui manípulos cólligit* should follow. |
